observations.label: INSTANCE THREE -- §8.8's sub-choice (single-verb accept-set) vs §14.3's widening; READY FOR A SCOPED §10 RULING
observations.status: FORCING FUNCTION MET. E08-04 ruled PROVISIONALLY pending it.
observations.cross_reference: C10-02, C14-04 (both batch 3); item E08-04; §8.8 SUB-CHOICE, §14.3, §3.4
observations.note:
INSTANCE THREE of §8.8's own SUB-CHOICE forcing function -- and the reviewer has ruled (2026-09-20) that three is the threshold at which this stops being a per-item judgment call and becomes a §10 question. PRIOR INSTANCES: C10-02 (real verb 'add' -> ESTABLISH, batch 3) and C14-04 (real verb 'perform ... to complete' -> PROCESS, batch 3). THIS INSTANCE: E08-04, real verb 'dispute', no near member at all.

WHAT §8.8 ITSELF SAYS, which is why this is a forcing function rather than a complaint. Its SUB-CHOICE paragraph is marked 'v0.24 default, pending confirmation' and states the problem in its own words: 'The single-verb accept-set means an extractor scores clause 2 correct only by picking the SAME near-miss the annotator picked; §14.4's objection to defaults partly applies.' It names the alternative -- an EMPTY action_accept_set, making every such item an automatic PARTIAL, 'more honest that no correct answer exists' but converting a measurement question into a guaranteed failure for roughly one item in four -- and says: 'Revisit once batch 3 supplies a second rate.' Batch 3 supplied two. This is the third.

THE EXACT TENSION, STATED PRECISELY because it is a conflict between two live rules and not a gap in either. §14.3 routes an ambiguity in an ACCEPT-SET field to the cheap resolution: 'If the ambiguity falls in an accept-set field (action §3.4, object_class §3.6): WIDEN THE ACCEPT-SET to cover every defensible reading. This is what accept-sets exist for, and it is the correct, cheap resolution.' §8.8's genuine-gap branch FORBIDS EXACTLY THAT: 'action_accept_set holds THAT VERB ALONE, no widening.' So the one cheap resolution the guideline offers is unavailable precisely where the annotator is least certain. C14-04's own annotator_notes record the collision hitting a real item and being resolved against §14.3: 'widening to include DELIVER was considered and rejected -- §8.8's sub-choice rule does not permit both tagging AND widening.' CITED BY NAME so the ruling session does not have to find it.

THE QUESTION FOR THE RULING, as the reviewer framed it: SHOULD A GENUINE-GAP TAG EVER COEXIST WITH A WIDENED ACCEPT-SET -- or is there a NARROWER FIX, e.g. permitting widening only among near-synonyms of the nearest verb rather than across the full accept-set? The narrow fix is worth stating as a distinct option because it preserves §8.8's real purpose (clause 2 must still measure whether extraction identified the action at all -- §8.8's 'why not generous accept-sets' paragraph) while removing the part §14.3 objects to.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THREE ITEMS. §8.8 measured the genuine-gap class at 23% of annotatable clauses, 95% Wilson CI [11%, 42%] -- 'about one gold item in four'. The sub-choice rule therefore governs the clause-2 outcome of roughly a quarter of the eventual 100-item set, and today it makes every one of them winnable only by coincidence of near-miss choice.

TODAY'S DISPOSITION IS PROVISIONAL AND SAYS SO. E08-04 is ruled PROCESS + action_not_in_taxonomy as an INTERIM answer (option (a)) so the batch is not blocked, explicitly pending this ruling -- the same discipline applied to the temporal_composition instances at C04-051/C04-072, which were logged as 'instance N' rather than resolved inside an annotation pass. If the ruling changes the sub-choice rule, E08-04 is revisited then. RESTAMPING WOULD BE FREE: no batch-4 segment has a cassette, so §22's conforming blocker does not attach.

READY FOR ITS OWN SCOPED RULING WHENEVER THERE IS APPETITE. SEARCH KEY: §8.8 sub-choice, single-verb accept-set, genuine gap widening, §14.3 vs §8.8, C10-02, C14-04, E08-04.
